hypothesis: States anywhere in binary64 are classified with the code unchanged through PLSR's power-of-two state scaling (components more than about 2^1022 below the largest one become subnormal in the scaled state and vanish beyond about 2^1075, which a code decided relative to |x|^2 does not see); matrices whose arithmetic leaves binary64 return NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW or an input refusal; no near-limit input yields a false certificate or a missed level-set exceedance.
input_data: A = [[-1, 2], [0, -3]], P = I with ten states from 2^-1074 to 1.797e308 (mixed scales included) and non-finite states
Near-limit matrices: A = -2^1000 I with P = 2^30 I; A = -2^511 I or -2^512 I with P = 2^511 I; P = 2^1022 I with x = (1.5, 1.5); affine A(theta) = -I + theta c I, theta = +-1e308
The subnormal witness A = [[-2, 5], [0, -3]] 2^-1074, P = I
mathematical_model: V(x) = x^T P x and x^T M x are homogeneous of degree two in x, so PLSR evaluates at x / 2^e with the unit state in [1, 2). The level gate decides V > level as scaled_value > level / s^2 and treats an infinite s^2 as 'exceeded' and a zero s^2 as 'not exceeded'. Exact truth: V = 2^(p + 2e) for P = 2^p I and x = 2^e e1.
numerical_result: 10 states from 2^-1074 to 1.797e308: 0 code changes (all CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN). Level scan (68 cases): 5 missed exceedances (certified with V > level, s^2 underflowed), 9 spurious exceedances (s^2 overflowed), 0 disagreements with the documented rule. Near-limit matrices: {'A=-2^1000 I, P=2^30 I': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW', 'A=-2^511 I, P=2^511 I': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', 'A=-2^512 I, P=2^511 I': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW', 'P=2^1022 I, x=(1.5, 1.5)': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW'}. theta overflow: {'theta:+1e308,c=1': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW', 'theta:-1e308,c=1': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW', 'theta:+1e308,c=2': 'raises ValueError'}. Subnormal witness: CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN. Conclusion: state scaling and matrix overflow behave as documented; the hypothesis is refuted by level-gate errors (missed, spurious), by an input error raised for an in-box theta, by a false certificate for a subnormal plant.
